title: Concurrency, queues, retries and silent loss

questions.text: What is the commit point? Name the line after which the work is durable. Is any done/seen/200 written before it?
What makes two of these the same, and which database constraint enforces it?
Where does this run, and what is its hard time limit? If the worst case is over it, it needs a queue or workflow with a status, not the request.
Who retries, how many times, with what backoff and budget? Exactly one layer. Which errors are not retryable?
If this runs twice at the same moment, or crashes halfway and restarts, what does the user see?
What proves the owner of a RUNNING row is alive (lease or heartbeat), and what moves it out when it is not?
Do long-lived references point at ids or at positions and copies? What version check stops a stale writer?
Draw the state machine, including approved, replaced and cancelled. What is every state's exit?
Does every tool or endpoint result say changed / unchanged / rejected / failed in a typed field, not only in prose?
Which shared resources (git refs, worktree, ports, build slot, DB rows, cache keys) does this touch that another agent or instance also touches? Pre-mortem: it ran twice and lost one; why?

budgets.measure: duplicate-effect query: GROUP BY idempotency key HAVING count(*) > 1
budgets.source: Stripe idempotency keys (2017); IETF Idempotency-Key draft

budgets.measure: RUNNING rows whose heartbeat is older than 2 leases
attempts per logical request from logs (retry ratio under 10% per client)

rules.title: Swallowed error (empty catch, or .catch that returns nothing)
rules.why: The failure disappears: the caller marks the item done and the sender never retries.
rules.confirm: failing-test: make the awaited call throw; assert the item is retried, failed or dead-lettered, never marked done
rules.fixHint: rethrow, or record the failure and let the single retry owner decide
knownFalsePositives: best-effort cleanup with a comment naming why loss is acceptable

rules.title: Swallowed error in Python (except: pass)
rules.why: Same as an empty catch: the error is gone and the work looks done.
rules.confirm: failing-test: raise inside the try; assert the outcome is a recorded failure
rules.fixHint: re-raise, or log with context and record a failed state

rules.title: Retry loop in a file with no backoff or jitter
rules.why: Fixed or zero delay retries in lockstep (thundering herd) and multiply load at every layer.
rules.confirm: failing-test: dependency returns 503 for 30 s under fake timers; assert attempts <= 1 + budget and delays grow
rules.fixHint: capped exponential backoff with full jitter, at one layer only

rules.title: Status set to DONE/SEEN/200 before the awaited work
rules.why: Success recorded before the effect is durable: a crash in between loses the item.
rules.confirm: failing-test: throw after the status write; assert the item is not left DONE

rules.title: findFirst/SELECT then create on the same key with no unique constraint or upsert
rules.why: Two concurrent runs both see nothing and both insert.
rules.confirm: failing-test: 3 concurrent calls via Promise.all; assert exactly one row

rules.title: Fire-and-forget promise (void call, .then without return/catch)
rules.why: The work can die silently and nobody records an outcome.
rules.confirm: repro-script: kill the process mid-run; count started vs finished records

rules.title: RUNNING/PROCESSING state with no heartbeat or lease column
rules.why: No reaper is possible, so a killed worker leaves the row RUNNING forever.
rules.confirm: failing-test: kill the worker after the side effect; assert retried or failed within lease + interval

rules.title: Persisted array index or position used as a cursor
rules.why: An insert before the cursor makes the next step skip or repeat.
rules.confirm: failing-test: complete step k, insert a step before k, advance; assert no skip and no repeat

rules.title: Timing constants related only by a comment
rules.why: Someone edits one value and the 'must stay below' relation breaks silently.

rules.title: Tool or endpoint returns prose ('ok', 'kept as is') with no typed outcome
rules.why: The caller (often a model) reads a no-op as success.
rules.confirm: repro-script: run the no-op path; show the reply cannot be told apart from success

verify.text: 3 concurrent deliveries of one payload -> exactly 1 effect
run(op); run(op) leaves the state equal to run(op) over generated inputs
kill the worker after the side effect -> row retried or failed within lease + interval, never stuck
throw after the commit-point candidate -> item retried or dead-lettered, never marked done
dependency 503 for 30 s -> attempts <= 1 + budget, delays growing with jitter
stuck-row, duplicate-effect and orphan-intent queries return 0
every non-terminal state has an exit (enum-driven test)
verify.tool: unit test / TLA+ for critical flows
